Natalie Fleet, the UK safeguarding minister, resigned after finding the work 'overwhelmingly triggering' due to her history as a survivor of abuse.

The Poison:
It is a tragedy that the nature of safeguarding work is so inherently traumatic that it prevents survivors from serving in the very roles they are best suited to understand.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
There is no plane error here. The actor correctly identified the conflict between their personal history (WHO) and the requirements of the role (WHAT).

Social Physics Analysis:
By choosing transparency over ego, the minister empowered the government to find a more suitable candidate. This is a clear example of prioritizing the mission over personal power.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The alignment of intent and action is nearly perfect.

The Unavoidable Truth: Some roles require a level of detachment that survivors of trauma may not be able to maintain.

The Unavoidable Lie: That stepping down is a sign of weakness rather than professional maturity.

This is a rare instance of structural honesty. By acknowledging the limits of her own capacity, the minister protected the efficacy of the safeguarding office.
